lead.headline: 944 for-profit nursing homes with operating companies formed 2022 to Sept 2024 rate 0.28 stars below same-state for-profit peers
lead.number: 52% are one- or two-star, 8 points above same-state for-profit homes; the median home sits 0.42 stars below
lead.watch_out: The company formation date only stands in for a sale and goes blank after Sept 2024; "worse after the change" did not survive matching (+0.9 citations, t about 1.5).

sources.outlet: Journal of the American Geriatrics Society (Ryskina et al.), abstract via Europe PMC
sources.quote: There was a small statistically significant decrease in 5-star ratings after a change in ownership (-0.09 points on a 5-point scale
Most acquired facilities showed indications of financial struggles, including lower star ratings and occupancy, plus a higher percentage of stays covered by Medicaid
Overall quality ratings decreased slightly with ownership change, by about 0.1 points on the 5-star scale.

sources.outlet: HHS Office of the Assistant Secretary for Planning and Evaluation (ASPE)
sources.quote: The ASPE analyses also found that SNFs with overall lower star quality ratings experience a change of ownership more often than SNFs with higher quality ratings.
By early 2026, star ratings for five of the nursing homes declined, with two of them dropping from five to two stars.
